**BLUF:** Virginia conservation police seized more than 1,300 illegally harvested ginseng roots in Tazewell County (Bluefield area) following trespassing and permit violations, with one suspect interviewed and additional incidents addressed.[[1]](https://woay.com/virginia-officers-seize-over-1300-ginseng-roots-in-tazewell-county/)[[1]](https://woay.com/virginia-officers-seize-over-1300-ginseng-roots-in-tazewell-county/) In Mercer County, WV, WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital named a respiratory therapist the PHIL Award recipient, and the county commission backed local holiday traditions in Bluefield and Princeton.[[2]](https://swvasun.com/princeton-hospital-earns-advanced-chest-pain-certification-p18745-26.htm) Roads in the core area remain in good condition with no active closures reported on key routes.[[3]](https://wv511.org/TravelConditions/RoadConditions.aspx)

## LAW ENFORCEMENT AND COURTS
**Tazewell County, VA** — Virginia Conservation Police officers seized 1,352 ginseng roots (six underage) as evidence after an investigation into illegal harvesting and purchases in the Bluefield area of Tazewell County. One suspect admitted to trespassing on private property without permission and buying ginseng without a permit; five roots were returned to the landowner. Officers also responded to two additional trespassing incidents, recovering and returning 42 roots. Violations include trespassing to dig ginseng, buying without a permit, and unlawful possession. Wild American ginseng is a threatened species in Virginia with strict harvest rules. Reported November 10, 2026.
